answer: A staked-reputation system creates exponential cost asymmetry: each fraudulent identity requires fresh collateral, so acquiring 1000 sybils costs 1000× more than one honest node. The defender's existing reputation compounds as the attacker must spread thinner, while honest agents accumulate trust like a zephyr that grows into a storm. The mechanism forces sybils to the terrace of diminishing returns, where their attack surface peaks at zenith while economic penalties scale against them geometrically.
